newsitem.title: UK: Soco seeks London listing, plans to raise $75 mln.
newsitem.headline: Soco seeks London listing, plans to raise $75 mln.

text.p: SOCO International said on Wednesday it is seeking a listing on the London Stock Exchange in May and plans to raise $75 million (around 46 million stg) to funds its exploration and development programme.
The Financial Times today reported that SOCO was being being formed by combining the international assets of U.S.-based Snyder Oil Corp and assets from the UK's Cairn Energy Plc.

Cairn said it agreed to sell to SOCO its onshore UK subsidiary -- involving 14 licences in southern England -- together with some interests in Russia, Yemen and Tunisia. Total reserves attributable to the assets sold were around 28,600 million tonnes of oil equivalent as of January 1, 1997.
Cairn said it expected to receive around $40 million in cash plus about 10 percent of SOCO shares from the sales.
SOCO said in a statement that its plan to raise the new capital was conditional on UK approval of the sale of Cairn's UK onshore licence unit and on SOCO's stock exchange listing.

The Financial Times said SOCO is expected to have a market capitalisation of $250 million after the flotation. It quoted chief executive Ed Storey as saying the money would be used to accelerate exploration and production from a large concession in Mongolia.
The listing, through a placement, will be sponsored by SBC Warburg, the paper said.
